profile.summary: Forecasting systems, GenAI products and high-performing data teams.

about.lead: For 9+ years I have taken machine learning from messy real-world data to production for enterprise clients.
body: At NielsenIQ I build price-forecasting models at scale on Databricks and PySpark, together with the test benches, guardrails and MLflow tracking that decide whether a run ships. At Saama I led a seven-person team delivering Unilever's trade promotion analytics country by country, and built an LLM assistant over Unilever's data.

Earlier work covers document understanding, computer vision and ground-truth datasets built from scratch for research at IISc. Away from the keyboard you will usually find me with a controller in hand: games keep my love for systems and strategy alive.

projects.title: car-agent-harness
projects.text: A used-car marketplace assistant that answers only through tools over the listings data, so it cannot invent cars or prices. Every change is scored by an eval suite in CI and blocked if quality drops.

projects.text: Shelf photo in, retail-audit report out: facings per shelf, empty slots, share of shelf and planogram compliance, as JSON a downstream system can trust.

projects.title: align-lab

projects.text: How fast and how cheap can an open LLM be served? Quantisation, speculative decoding, caching and llm-d routing on Kubernetes, with cost per million tokens for each setup.

projects.title: demand-forecast-pipeline
projects.text: Weekly retail demand forecasting run by Airflow: retrain, compare challenger against champion, promote only if better, and publish a dashboard with a written summary.

projects.title: Binary-classification-of-audio
projects.text: Sudden-sound (gunshot) detection: a CNN on MFCC features trained on UrbanSound8K, served by a Flask API that takes an audio or video URL, packaged as a Docker image.

work.title: Forecast at scale: price forecasting with validation gates
work.text: Forecasts that feed client decisions across many product categories. A wrong forecast costs more than a slow one, so the work was as much about catching bad output as producing good output.
points: Introduced ML models for price forecasting, and a traffic-light system that classifies product performance so business users can act faster.
Added post-processing guardrails and a test-bench framework that validates every run.
Integrated MLflow for experiment tracking and model management; added logging for faster root-cause analysis.
Replaced legacy engines and the licensed NAG library with scalable Python and PySpark.
work.approach: Every run is checked by the test bench and the guardrails, and every experiment is recorded in MLflow, so a model change can be compared and explained rather than argued about.

work.title: Trade Area Model: legacy C++ to modular Python
work.text: A production model on a legacy C++ codebase that was hard to maintain and extend. The task: move it to Python without losing what it did well, and make its outputs easier to interpret.
points: Led the migration from C++ to Python, improving maintainability and scalability.
Designed coefficient-extraction models that make results interpretable for downstream analytics.
Contributed to a modular modelling framework that new models can plug into.

work.title: Trade promotion analytics: multi-country rollout
work.text: Unilever needed to know which promotions actually work. The platform estimates demand, price elasticity and cannibalization from sales data, adapted to each country's market and data.
points: Led a team of seven and was the main technical contact for client stakeholders.
Built the demand, price-elasticity and cannibalization models at the core of the platform.
Rolled out country by country, with per-country features and parameters tracked in MLflow.
Wrote validation and sanity checks for input sales data and every model's output.
work.approach: Every country release passed input-data checks and output sanity checks before it reached the client, and elasticity coefficients were tracked in MLflow so changes between runs could be explained.

work.title: LLM / RAG data assistant
work.text: Trade promotion users needed answers from a large body of internal data without waiting on an analyst: a conversational assistant grounded in their own data.
points: Built the assistant on LangChain with ChatGPT, answering data questions in natural language.
Indexed internal data in Azure Cognitive Search and wired retrieval into the chain.
Deployed it as a web app next to the users' existing workflow.
work.approach: Started from the questions users asked again and again, grounded every answer in retrieved internal content rather than the model's own knowledge, and shipped it where users already worked.

work.title: Computer vision APIs for a product platform
work.text: A product platform needed recognition and insight services its team could call directly, plus dashboards over the data they produced.
points: Built face recognition (FaceNet), place recognition, and bike-accessory detection with brand identification (YOLO).
Built NER-based NLP services, all served through Flask on AWS.
Delivered Power BI reporting that harmonised Salesforce, PeopleSoft and spreadsheet sources.

work.title: Document information extraction
work.text: Turn scanned invoices, bills and balance sheets into structured fields that downstream systems can consume without manual data entry.
points: Built one extraction model per document type, each trained on its own labelled dataset.
Created the ground truth: entities and intents defined per document family.
Built the OCR stage, trained RASA NLU entity models and served JSON output for client integration.
work.approach: One model per document family instead of one generic model, so each could be tuned and checked against its own labelled dataset.

work.title: Deep-learning resume parser
work.text: Resumes arrive in every layout imaginable. The goal: reliably pull personal details, work history and education out of them as structured entities.
points: Two stages: a segmentation model splits the document into sections, then three dedicated entity models.
Built a dataset per model and trained the LSTM entity models; a test bench checked every dataset before training.
Served through a Flask API with JSON output.
work.approach: Splitting the problem, segment first and then extract per section, let each model specialise; the test bench caught dataset problems before they became model problems.

work.title: Multispectral imagery: segmentation from scratch
work.text: Vegetation analysis from satellite and drone imagery, where no labelled dataset existed to train on.
points: Stitched UAV multispectral imagery and annotated it to build the ground truth.
Created a 5-class dataset from ISRO satellite images and built a custom segmentation model.
Benchmarked VGG16, ResNet and SharpMask against it.
